notes.title: Fireside Chat: August Update!
notes.notes:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39919619/bece024a054045e3cadc11a5805ddd2faa55704f.jpg"]
Hello Hikers! Another month finished, time for another Fireside Chat!

August FLEW by so quick it was actually a bit scary. We started this month off with our first of many tutorial videos! We aim to cover all the essential systems we have implemented and we've already completed 2 videos. More to come soon! I know we mention this a lot, but as a small team we have to maintain a fine balance so these videos will take a bit of time. 

Another exciting update on our end is we did talk to EPIC! We had a long call with them talking about everything related to optimization. We've received extensive documentation and we'll cover more about this soon.

We will also address the elephant in the room, which is both "when is the next DEMO update" and "When is the game releasing". We're implementing our new MULTIPLAYER system which offers a new way to create a lobby and then join the game as a lobby. This new system makes sure that once the HOST is fully loaded in, all other players in the lobby will start loading in. We're also neck deep in optimization work, with all the help from EPIC we've found a lot that we've already optimized and we have a ton more in the works. We're also building out FALL, squashing bugs and working on new features. Again, as a small team this is a lot to balance, but we're doing the best we can.

"When will the game be released?" - We will have more in depth information on this very soon, our goal is the get this game to be playable for as many people as possible, and with this help from EPIC we are making strides towards that.

What we want as a studio is to continue being transparent with you, our amazing community. We see the feedback, we see all the love you send our way and we see that we've got a great game on our hands here. Great games get one chance to prove they're great, and we aim to come out as solid as we can with an extensive plan on what we're doing AFTER Early Access launch. 

That was all for this monthly Fireside Chat, talk more soon!

notes.title: Fireside Chat: July Update + Meet the Team
notes.notes:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39919619/aab6c40780c5dae3ce216a359316807e139c2c64.png"]

Hello hello, Hikers!

It’s the end of the month and time for a new community update and this time with a new name. Welcome to the monthly Fireside Chat!

First and foremost, we want to thank everyone again for the continued support and feedback. We say it all the time but we mean it every time. Because of you, we’ve hit so many exciting milestones and we can’t wait to reach more with you!

This past month has been another busy month of patches on the Demo and our push toward Early Access! While we’ve got a lot done, there is still a lot more we’re continuing to work through and as always, we’ll keep you updated here as well as Discord and Trello.

We also wanted to take a moment to introduce ourselves. We often mention that Fairview Games is a core team of 6 but we haven’t talked about WHO Fairview Games is. So without further ado, meet the core Fairview Games team!

Craig Martin - Co-Founder, Lead Engineer

While many of you may know Craig for his “excellent” navigation skills, he is also one of the Co-Founders of Fairview Games and Lead Engineer on The Gold River Project. You got a bug? Craig can fix it!

David Parkes - Co-Founder, Lead Game Design

Known by many in the community as the guy with the voice of a radio host, Dave is the other Co-Founder of Fairview Games and Lead Game Design on The Gold River Project! The beautiful world many of you have experienced is in large part from the mind of Dave!

Stephen Parkes - Lead Art Design

Dave’s equally creative brother, Steve, is another HUGE part of the beauty of the world of The Gold River Project as Lead Art Design! In addition to the beautiful landscapes in game, you can find his work in other designs such as the game’s logo and Steam cover art!

Bobby Hughes - Lead Technical Artist

Some of you may know Bobby from our Dev Livestreams as Craig’s Camp parent. When he’s not wrangling Craig on the trail, Bobby spends his time helping Craig wrangle bugs and implement fun new systems in the game. Without Bobby, we wouldn’t have cool systems like Farming!

Joakim Elseberg - Community Management

The King of Discord! Joakim, or as you all know him, Jokka, is a Community Manager for The Gold River Project. He’s often found in Discord and post replies helping out our community in whatever way he can! He is a real Mensch.

Samantha Nye - Marketing and Community Management

The narrator of this post! I work alongside Jokka on Community and social media stuff as well as general Marketing for The Gold River Project. I do a lot of work behind the scenes but you can also find me on Discord, our Social Media, and here on Steam!

Being a small team, in addition to our primary roles, we all wear many hats. Making a game is a team effort and this team, frankly, is having a lot of fun making it and we’re really excited to see where the trail we’re on with this takes us. Until next time!

Happy Hiking!

notes.title: June Community Update: What's Next?
notes.notes:
Happy Monday, Hikers!

June flew by but it’s time for our monthly Community Update.

This past month has been an incredibly busy but incredibly fulfilling time. We kicked off with a successful Steam Next Fest. As a small team, getting a game out in the wild is not only a big accomplishment, but a scary one at that. As developers, we want to make a game people enjoy and regardless of how excited we are, it’s hard to know how others will respond. Needless to say, we were overwhelmed by such a positive response to the Alpha Demo. Again, thank you for all your support!

So what’s next?

If you haven’t had a chance to play the Demo yet or even if you have and want to continue playing, have no fear, we will be keeping it up! We want to make sure people are still able to enjoy this snippet of our world as much as they’d like. In addition to all the positive feedback we’ve received, we’ve also been able to learn where improvement is needed and will continue to patch and update the Demo!

Even more excitingly, as we’ve been patching the Demo, we have also continued our work toward Early Access release! While we have no official date, we will be continuing our push for an Early Access release late Summer 2025! As we continue squashing bugs, implementing feedback, and expanding our world, optimization and fun remain our #1 priority and we want to ensure we can deliver as much as possible. We hope you’re ready for more seasons, more enemies, and more mysteries to solve.

We can’t wait to get to share so much more with you all soon! Stay tuned! In the meantime, be sure to join our Discord. We're around to answer any questions, comments, and concerns :).

notes.title: May Community Update: A Special Thank You
notes.notes:
Hello Hikers! 

May is coming to an end which means it’s time for our monthly update! With the official release of the Demo, it has been an absolutely incredible month so this update is going to be a bit different.

This month, we simply wanted to say thank you. Releasing a Demo is always scary, especially for a small Indie team. The feedback we have gotten so far has been beyond what we imagined and we are so excited to see everyone’s enthusiasm! It has always been and continues to be our goal to make a game that people would enjoy and seeing and hearing everyone’s first impressions has been fulfilling! 

In addition to all the positive feedback, we’ve also received SO much valuable feedback! Every bug report, Discord ticket, and screenshot shared has helped us so much. We cannot thank you all enough for not just playing, but for taking the time to share your experiences. On top of that, we are floored by all the videos and streams! Not only are we thankful to see you all wanting to share our game with your audiences, but your videos and streams have been incredibly helpful in finding bugs and room for improvement (and having extra fun doing it). 

In the first week, we’ve reached over 20k wishlists and 10k Demo downloads. Again, the response has been so much more than we expected and we can’t thank each and every one of you enough. We are so incredibly lucky.

As more of you play the Demo, we’ll continue implementing the feedback on our way to Early Access release later this Summer! Until then, we’ll see you around.

Happy Hiking!

notes.title: April Community Update: New Map and Features
notes.notes:
Hello hello again, Hikers!

April has come to an end and it’s time to recap what we’ve been working on. It’s been a big month with some real big changes so we have a lot to share!

Brand New Map

The Gold River Project’s development originally began about 3 years ago on Unreal Engine 4. As time went on, development progressed, and we began moving development to Unreal Engine 5, we ran into some issues that hurt performance. So, in addition to the various adjustments in March, we’ve also moved to a brand new map created from real locations in the Pacific Northwest using World Creator and imported it to UE 5.4. In turn, we were able to not only improve performance, but got to make the map look even better (Look at all those trees and mountains!).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39919619/ed8c26b7ae6263c7efa14e69254d2f2315a9e074.png

New Features

As we moved to the new map, we also added new gameplay features to deepen the experience.


 Drink Water from Streams and Lakes - We’ve expanded the ways to hydrate! Now, instead of only being able to replenish your hydration with the water bottles you may find on your adventures, you can now drink from streams and lakes! But be careful. Just like the real wilderness, drinking straight from the source may make you sick. You’ll want to learn how to clean contaminated water to avoid making your trip even more dangerous.
 Twinkle Twinkle Little Lights - It looks like you’re going to be stuck out here for a while. So why not make camp a little more comfortable? You can give your campsite a little flair by crafting Twinkle Lights to decorate!
 Sit and Rest - Exploring the wilderness and fighting for your life will take a lot out of you! We’ve added a sit and rest mechanic that will enable you to build up your stamina to prepare you for your daily scavenges! Just pull up a chair, sit by the fire, and rest. Note: If you continue sitting even after your stamina bar is full, you can build one additional bar to buy you even more time! 

While April was a big month in development, May is about to be even bigger. We have some very big announcements coming VERY soon so stay tuned! The adventure of a lifetime is just ahead ;).

Happy Hiking!

- The Fairview Games Team

notes.title: March Community Update: Backer Testing and Optimization
notes.notes:
Hey Hikers!


It’s been an extra busy year for the Fairview Games team as we quickly make our way through some big milestones and all the things we need to do to get The Gold River Project out to you all. As we quickly approach this goal, we’re starting monthly Dev Blogs to keep you up to date and get a peek behind the curtain to learn more about our team and game!

Our biggest priority is creating a fun & dynamic game as many people as possible can play. Months of testing with our Backers has lead to a ton of improvements to gameplay and LOTS of bug fixes. Also very importantly, it has helped us pinpoint optimization needs to help us get the game running on as many PC builds as possible. While this goal is still a work in progress, we’ve already made a ton of improvements! Here is what we’ve done so far:



 Reduced texture sizes to save on VRAM and reduce game size
 Pinpointed character model details that were causing loss of frames
 Updated game UI
 Pinpointed pain points in gameplay that were leading to frame drops
 Overall map adjustments to reduce demand on machines


With all of these adjustments, we’ve already gotten reports of improvements from Backers! While we have some temporary solutions in place, knowing we’ve found the causes brings us that much closer to a more playable game!

Tackling community updates, marketing, and game development with a team of 6 is a challenge, but a rewarding one. Community and player experience are important to us and we’re going to keep doing everything we can to bring you a game you all can thoroughly enjoy. And at the pace we’re going, that could be sooner than you think. Hope 2025 works for you all too 😉.

We’re hoping to make this a big year for us! Thank you for joining us on this journey.

See you all again soon! 

The Fairview Games Team
